Aromatic

air-uh-MAT-ik -- stress on the third syllable, MAT. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Aromatic is having a pleasant or distinctive smell.

An aromatic cloud of fresh-baked bread drifted from the bakery door and stopped commuters mid-stride.

Worked Example

She pries the lid off her grandmother's old spice tin, and the scent of cinnamon and cardamom instantly fills the whole kitchen.

Spices whose scent announces itself that vividly are aromatic -- they carry a pleasant, distinctive smell. The word is almost always a compliment to whatever your nose notices first.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

fragrant: Fragrant means giving off a sweet, pleasing smell -- fragrant roses, fragrant soap. Aromatic adds character to the pleasure: the smell is rich and distinctive, announcing exactly what it is, the way coffee or cedar does. Everything aromatic smells good; fragrant does not promise a scent you could name.

perfumed: Perfumed means treated with fragrance on purpose -- air, paper, or skin deliberately loaded with sweetness, sometimes to excess. Aromatic praises the smell a thing gives off naturally: herbs, fresh bread, cut wood. A perfumed glove got its scent from a bottle; an aromatic loaf earned its own.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

odorless: having no smell at all

musty: smelling stale, damp, and old

Where it sits · how strongly the smell fills the air — scented → aromatic → overpowering

scented vs. aromatic: Scented is the mildest of the family -- scented paper merely carries a light smell, while something aromatic has a rich, distinctive scent that fills the air around it.

overpowering vs. aromatic: Overpowering goes beyond aromatic into too much: an aromatic room smells rich and pleasant, while an overpowering one is so thick with scent that it drives people out.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — aromat-

root — aromat-: spice, sweet smell (Greek aroma, whose stem is aromat-, via Latin)

suffix — -ic

suffix — -ic: having the characteristics of; like (Greek -ikos, via Latin -icus)

Put it together

Put it together: Aromatic is aroma -- Greek for 'spice, sweet smell,' whose stem is aromat- -- plus -ic: 'having the characteristics of an aroma.' Anything aromatic behaves like a spice, announcing itself to your nose before anything else.

Use the root in a new word: aromatherapy

Use the root in a new word: aromatherapy: The spa's aromatherapy session used lavender oil to help guests unwind.

Root Check

Word Choice

Aromatic leans positive and distinctive -- aromatic herbs, aromatic coffee, aromatic cedar. For bad smells English reaches for other words entirely, so calling something aromatic is nearly always praise for how it greets the nose. Note that aromatherapy is a modern compound of aroma + therapy; aroma does not share a root with therapy.
